subject: Split-path causing drops on private backhaul — security rule mismatch
messages:
From: Mountain Health NetOps <netops@mountainhealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packet drops seen on private backhaul to our data center

Hi Diego,

We're seeing intermittent downstream packet drops from your private edge into our on-prem environment since last night (~23:00 UTC). Symptoms:
- Connections from Redwood-hosted instances to our internal database time out after ~30s.
- Traceroutes show the return path switches to a different egress midway.
- Attaching traceroute output and a short pcap that captures a timeout and a retransmit spike.

Can your team triage? We're blocked on our staging tests for tomorrow's cutover.

Attachments: mh-traceroute-0809.txt (text), mh-pcap-downstream-0809.pcap (pcap)

Thanks,
J. Lopez
Mountain Health — NetOps

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Mountain Health NetOps <netops@mountainhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packet drops seen on private backhaul to our data center

Thanks for the data, J. — we're on it.

Quick notes from an initial look: your traceroute shows an asymmetric return after hop 4 which aligns with the retransmit bursts in the pcap. That typically points to either a SNAT/eBPF policy causing replies to egress via a different transit or an ACL/SG on your edge dropping traffic when source ports change.

Marissa/Karthik — can you pull the edge security group snapshot and recent NAT table entries for the timeframe 2026-08-08 22:30 UTC -> 2026-08-09 00:30 UTC? Also please check whether any path-based route changes (BGP/route-map) were applied overnight.

J., we'll keep you updated in this thread. If we need a maintenance window to apply a policy-based route or temporary SNAT rule, we'll propose times below.

Diego
Diego Fernandez
SRE, Private Deployments — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mountain Health NetOps <netops@mountainhealth.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packet drops seen on private backhaul to our data center

On initial pull: attaching SG snapshot and NAT table from the private-edge that terminates the cross-connect.

Observed:
- Security group attached to the on-prem-facing interface had an ingress rule that allowed TCP 0-65535 from Mountain Health subnets, but an egress rule set was inadvertently tightened yesterday to only allow established flows to our provider-facing pool. That can drop packets when replies appear to come from an unexpected source when SNAT occurs.
- NAT state shows translations for ephemeral ports that are being rewritten; however, we see a secondary path advertised by our transit partner that causes replies to exit through a different device which lacks the same SG context.

Attachments: edge-sg-snapshot-0809.json (JSON)

Immediate next steps I recommend:
1) Add a temporary egress rule on the on-prem-facing interface to explicitly allow return traffic from our transit ASN / provider-facing IP space for the Mountain Health subnets.
2) Put in a policy-based SNAT that preserves the original source interface for flows bound to Mountain Health's prefixes.
3) Coordinate with Mountain Health to confirm they will not apply a restrictive firewall change on their side during the window.

I'll draft the remediation commands and a short rollback plan. Suggest we schedule a 30-minute window tonight 02:00–02:30 UTC if that works for your team.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Network Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: J. Lopez <j.lopez@mountainhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packet drops seen on private backhaul to our data center

Thanks Marissa — that aligns with what we see. Our firewall team did tighten egress rules yesterday as part of a microsegmentation change, but they denied impact at the time. We're happy to hold a maintenance slot tonight 02:00–02:30 UTC.

I'll ask AWS enterprise to standby in case transit-level changes are required (cc'ing them).

-J.

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mountain Health NetOps <netops@mountainhealth.com>, AWS Enterprise Support <aws-enterprise@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packet drops seen on private backhaul to our data center

Good morning — posted the remediation playbook to the shared drive and drafted the commands below for the on-edge device (synthesized for our platform and the partner appliance):

-- Remediation excerpt (dry-run first):
1) add ip route policy for Mountain Health prefixes -> prefer interface A (policy-based route):
   sudo ip rule add from <redwood-subnet> to <mountainhealth-prefix> lookup 200 pref 1000
   ip route add default via <transit-next-hop> dev ethA table 200

2) apply SNAT-preserve for flows bound to Mountain Health:
   nft add table nat
   nft add chain nat postrouting { type nat hook postrouting priority 100; }
   nft add rule nat postrouting ip saddr <redwood-subnet> ip daddr <mountainhealth-prefix> counter snat to <provider-ip> preserve-ports

3) add temporary egress allow on on-prem interface for provider ASN / IPs

If the PBR + SNAT preserve steps are applied, replies should stay symmetric. If we still see asymmetry, AWS support may need to adjust route advertisements at the transit level.

I've scheduled the runbook and attached a one-page rollback in the drive. Please confirm the 02:00–02:30 UTC window and I'll coordinate the change with infra and AWS.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Network Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packet drops seen on private backhaul to our data center

Thanks everyone — plan is approved.

Action items:
- 02:00–02:30 UTC maintenance window tonight (2026-08-11) confirmed by Mountain Health.
- Karthik/Marissa to apply PBR + SNAT-preserve during the window, validate with active traceroutes and pcap sampling.
- If asymmetry persists, AWS will be asked to withdraw the alternate advertisement for the session (NET-4923).
- Diego to monitor metrics and post a 1-hr and 6-hr follow-up summary.

I've uploaded the remediation playbook and attached the short PDF for your records. Please ACK once remediation is complete so we can close the ticket.

Diego Fernandez
